family: collect/expand counter with drains; growth cycle
summary: Two blocks trade places, about 7 times longer each round, until the left one is drained into the block at the right end; from step 1.8·1015 on the run repeats exactly every 116,320,154 visits of the left end with the right block 321,042,928 words longer, so it never halts. Proved in Lean: a symbolic executor with a soundness proof replays the arrival and one period for every odd length (compiled evaluation, native_decide).
title: What is known about 1RB0RC_0RC1RC_0LD0RA_1LE0LF_0LA1LC_---1LA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RC_0RC1RC_0LD0RA_1LE0LF_0LA1LC_---1LA.
intro: This six-state, two-symbol Turing machine is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. It does not halt when started on a blank tape; the proof is in Lean, with its two long computations evaluated by compiled code. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: It does not halt (Lean theorem nonhalt, level native). From step 1,818,198,163,340,705 on, the configuration E> 0 (1011001)^59 1011 00000 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r comes back with r larger by 321,042,928 after 116,320,154 arrivals at the left end, for every odd r ≥ 65. In Lean, a symbolic executor whose every move is proved to be a run of the machine (kernel) replays the arrival from blank tape and one period with r = 65 + 2x, x free; the two replays and the twelve cycle rules they use are evaluated by native_decide, so the result rests on the Lean kernel and the Lean compiler. The exact step and visit counts are computed by the Python and C++ simulators (trusted), not part of the Lean statement.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 43,491 cells have been visited and 26,502 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478).

claims.title: Sweeps over the long blocks
claims.text: L A>(0011011)^n R → L (1100110)^n A> R (13n steps), L (1011001)^n D>1 R → L D>1 (0110110)^n R (23n steps), L A>(011)^n R → L (110)^n A> R (3n steps), for every n, L, R.

claims.title: The two long phases, any number of cycles
claims.text: Collecting: E> 0 (1011001)^p (101)^5 10 (011)^q 000 (011)^r (q even, r odd) becomes the same with p + 2n, q − 2n. Expanding: E> 0 (1011001)^p 1011 0^5 110110011010 (101)^m 1000 (011)^r (m even, r odd) becomes the same with p − 2n, m + 14n. One cycle each with its exact step count (48a + 48b + 72p + 476 and 240b + 240c + 144p + 2812), n cycles by induction.

claims.title: The machine does not halt
claims.text: From blank tape the machine never reaches a halting configuration: nonhalt : ¬ HaltsFromBlank. It combines the three claims below with nonhalting_of_growth_cycle. Axioms used: propext, Quot.sound and 14 compiled evaluations (native_decide): the two replays and the twelve cycle rules.

claims.title: The machine does not halt: a second proof, in Coq (busycoq)
claims.text: The same argument, ported to Coq on top of busycoq's definitions: nonhalt : ~ halts tm c0. The symbolic executor is proved sound against busycoq's step, and all runs are evaluated inside Coq's kernel by vm_compute; Print Assumptions nonhalt reports no axioms. Clean build with Coq 8.18.0: about 40 s.

claims.title: A growth cycle implies non-halting
claims.text: With C(r) = E> 0 (1011001)^59 1011 00000 1101100110110 (011)^16 001101100110 (011)^r: if the run from blank tape reaches some C(65 + 2x), and every C(65 + 2x) reaches C(65 + 2(x + 160,521,464)) in at least one step, the machine does not halt from blank tape. The two hypotheses are proved by the replay below.

claims.title: A symbolic executor, proved sound
claims.text: Tapes are lists of cells and blocks (w)^n with n = c + a0x0 + a1x1 + …, the x free. A move is a shift rule from a table (a block crossed at once, one or two copies at a time), or one machine step, and at each arrival of state E at the left end a re-bracketing of the tape and a cycle rule applied N times at once. Any step that would depend on a variable fails. Theorem: if the executor goes from S to S′ in k moves and its tables are valid, the machine goes from S to S′ for every value of the variables. The 31 shift rules are proved by evaluation in the kernel; the N-fold application of a cycle rule by induction.

claims.title: Twelve cycle rules, for all values of their counts
claims.text: Each rule says: this tape with counts bi + 2xi comes back with counts bi + Di + 2xi, for all xi (eleven are collect or expand, plain or with inert zones in between, 2 or 4 visits; one is the drain, 72 visits, 201,007 executor moves). Each is one run of the executor without cycle rules, evaluated by native_decide.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches C(16,797,709)
claims.text: 5,037,044 moves of the executor from blank tape end at C(16,797,709) (arrive_run, native_decide, 13 s); by soundness the machine reaches that configuration.

claims.title: C(65 + 2x) reaches C(65 + 2(x + 160,521,464)), for every x
claims.text: 5,581,714 moves of the executor from C(65 + 2x), x a free variable, end at C(321,042,993 + 2x) (period_run, native_decide, 14 s); by soundness the machine does so for every x, in at least one step.

claims.title: The growth cycle: visit and step counts
claims.text: C(r) reaches C(r + 321,042,928) after 116,320,154 arrivals at the left end and 650,373,336,347,246,654 + 4,382,930,856 (r − 65) steps. That C(r) reaches C(r + 321,042,928) is a Lean theorem (above); the counts come from two symbolic simulators that agree (py/closure/accel.py and the model of the Lean executor, py/replay/engine.py), checked against numeric runs from C(65), C(67), C(79) and three periods of the real run; 17 injected defects are all reported.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches the cycle: step counts
claims.text: That blank tape reaches C(16,797,709) is a Lean theorem (above). The step counts are computed: the run is at C(16,797,709) after 1,818,198,163,340,705 steps (event 6,086,451), and at C(337,840,637) after 725,814,446,706,290,623 steps. The word-level engine agrees with a plain C simulator at all 24,646 events of the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps (step count and CRC of the tape).

claims.title: Neighbouring classes halt
claims.text: The same pattern with 61 words in the left block halts for every odd r ≥ 65, after 1,772,276 + 5,220 (r − 65) steps (confirmed by plain simulation for r = 65, 67, 71); C(r) with r even ≥ 64 halts at its 21,362,421st event. So the real run is safe only because of the exact orbit it is on.

claims.title: Independent check of the growth cycle
claims.text: A second accelerated simulator, written from scratch without reading the first (verify/sim3.cpp, validated against plain simulation to 1010 steps), lands exactly on C(16,797,709) at step 1,818,198,163,340,705 from blank tape, and takes C(r) exactly to C(r + 321,042,928) at the predicted step for r = 65, 67, …, 85 and r = 16,797,709. It also confirms that C(r) halts for the even r tried (the halting transition is one step after the count stated in the notes: that count excludes the halting step). It checks listed values only; “for every odd r” is the Lean theorem grow_cyc.

explainer.lede: It never halts, and Lean proves it. Two blocks of the tape trade places, about seven times longer each round; now and then the left block is poured into a third block at the far right. After 1.8·10<sup>15</sup> steps the whole pattern repeats exactly, with only that third block longer each time.

facts.text: Lean theorem nonhalt; two replays and twelve rules evaluated by compiled code.
The symbolic executor that does the replays is proved sound in Lean.
From step 1.8·10<sup>15</sup> the run repeats every 116,320,154 visits of the left end, the right block 321,042,928 words longer (the counts are computed, the return is proved).
The last step of the argument, proved in Lean.
Injected defects reported by the cycle checker.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: From six states to one number
html: The question "does this machine halt?" can be asked at four levels of description. Each level keeps less detail
than the one above it, and each step down is a theorem saying that the answer is the same. The page walks down the
ladder: the six-state machine on its tape; the tape read as blocks of repeated words at the moments state E reaches
the left end; whole cycles of the long phases, each a rule that holds for every size of the blocks; and finally one
number r, the length of the last block, which grows by 321,042,928 every period and never leads to a halt.
A tape of cells and a head in one of six states. One unit of time is one step.
Kernel no halt in 10,000 steps
native_decide no halt in 107 steps (blank_runs_native)
Level 2Blocks of words
The tape as cells and blocks (w)^n, looked at when state E reaches the left end (an event). One unit is one move of the executor: a whole block crossed by a shift rule, or one step.
Kernel same answer as level 1: run_sound, the 31 shift rules shRTbl_ok, shLTbl_ok
Level 3Cycles of the phases
A whole-tape template with counts b + 2x that comes back with counts b' + 2x after 2, 4 or 72 events. One unit is one cycle; N cycles are one move.
native_decide twelve cycle rules for all x: rule0_ok … rule11_ok
Kernel N cycles at once: rule_instN
Level 4The growth cycle C(r)
One number r. C(65 + 2x) comes back as C(65 + 2(x + 160,521,464)). One unit is one period, 116,320,154 events.
Kernel the cycle implies no halt: nonhalting_of_growth_cycle
Pick an event. The browser runs the real machine from blank tape up to that moment and reads its tape. The rows
show the same instant at each level: the cells, the blocks of words, the cycle rule of the Lean proof whose template
the tape fits (if any), and where the moment sits on the way to the growth cycle. Where a rule fits, the browser
also runs the machine on to the end of the rule's cycle and checks that it arrives exactly where the rule says.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.498). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.478).
After 109 steps the tape spans 43,491 cells (12,594 left of the start, 17,410 right), with a density of 1s of 0.609.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Seven-cell words on the left, three-cell words on the right
html: Look at the tape each time the head, in state E, reaches the left end of the visited tape: an event. The
tape is then a block of seven-cell words 1011001, a short irregular zone, and then blocks of the
three-cell word 011 separated by a few zeros. The last block, (011)^r, ends the tape.
Going right, the head shifts a block of three-cell words by one cell (3 steps a word). Going left, it crosses two
words at a time (18 steps). So what happens at the end of a block depends only on whether its length is even or odd:
every cycle rule the proof needed has the form "for all lengths of this parity".
The Lean proof works at this level with a symbolic executor: a program whose tape is a list of cells and
blocks (w)^n, where n may be c + a x with x unknown. One move of the executor either crosses
a whole block with a shift rule, or makes one ordinary step (opening a block only when its count is surely
at least 1). A shift rule says: in state q, with the word u just behind the head, the head crosses k copies of a word
w and leaves the word v behind it, in s steps, without looking at anything else. Each of the 31 shift rules is a
Lean statement about the machine for every tape around those cells, checked by the kernel
run_sound (lean/Exec.lean, kernel) says that whatever the executor does in some number of
moves, the machine does, for every value of the unknowns. That is the theorem that makes level 2 answer the same as
<input type="text" class="rc-num" id="rcs-n" value="5" inputmode="numeric" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="off">

The rule holds if the head never reads a random cell, ends in state q at the far side, and the cells read u vn as the rule says. Words are written nearest cell first, as in the Lean file, so on the left of the head they appear reversed.

sections.heading: Collect, expand, drain
html: Three regular phases take almost all the time. p counts the seven-cell words, q or m the three-cell words of the
middle block, r those of the last block.
<div style="overflow-x:auto"><table class="tbl"><thead><tr><th>phase</th><th>tape when state E reaches the left end</th><th>one cycle</th></tr></thead><tbody>
collect0 (1011001)^p (101)^5 10 (011)^q 000 (011)^r, q even, r odd2 events: p + 2, q − 2
expand0 (1011001)^p 1011 0^5 110110011010 (101)^m 1000 (011)^r, m even, r odd4 events: p − 2, m + 14
Collecting turns three-cell words into seven-cell words one for one; expanding gives seven three-cell words back
for each seven-cell word. So each round the blocks are about seven times longer: about 600, 4,370, 30,750, 215,000,
1,506,000 words. Between the phases there are short irregular stretches where the separators collide, and trains of
cars (011)^4 0 are built and taken apart. Usually the next round starts. Sometimes the stretch ends in
the drain pattern: then the whole left block is poured into the last block (414 words of three for 52 words of
seven), and the left part starts again from a small state, in front of a much longer last block.
At level 3 a whole cycle of a phase is one statement. A cycle rule is a template of the whole tape whose
counts are b + 2x before and b' + 2x after, one x for each block that changes. It is proved
for all values of the x by one run of the executor itself, without cycle rules, from the template before to the
template after (ruleOK_of_run, kernel; the run is evaluated by native_decide:
a rule N times in one move, N as large as the shrinking counts allow; the induction over N is in Lean
(rule_instN, kernel), so the choice of N is not trusted. Twelve rules were enough: eleven are collect or
expand, plain or with inert trains in between, and one, rule 8, is the drain. Separately, lean/Phases.lean
proves the plain collect and expand cycles by hand for any number of cycles, with the kernel only
<input type="text" class="rc-num" id="rcr-x" value="2" inputmode="numeric" spellcheck="false" autocomplete="off">

Every block that has a variable gets the same x here. The browser writes the template on a blank tape, puts the head on its first cell in state E, runs the real machine until state E has reached the left end the rule's number of times, and compares the tape with the template after. The drain (rule 8) takes about five million steps. lean/Phases.lean writes the blocks of three-cell words with the six-cell word 110110 and allows any count b + x, not only b + 2x.

sections.heading: The left part comes back to the same state
html: The left part of the tape never needs more of the last block than the parity of its length, and a drain adds an
even number of words. After the second drain the left part reaches a state that it meets again, exactly, two drains
Events and steps computed by the simulators (py/closure/accel.py, py/replay/engine.py, verify/sim3.cpp, which agree); the Lean statement does not count them.
One period is two epochs, two drains. To prove that it goes on for ever, one period is run with r replaced by
65 + 2x, x unknown. Whenever a step would depend on the value of x the executor stops; it never had to.
It ends in the same configuration with 65 + 321,042,928 + 2x, after 5,581,714 moves
run_pos this is the theorem grow_cyc: for every x, C(65 + 2x) reaches C(65 + 2(x +
160,521,464)) in at least one step. The run from blank tape reaches C(16,797,709) = C(65 + 2·8,398,822)
(reach_cyc: 5,037,044 moves, lean/Arrive.lean). And the kernel proves the last step,
nonhalting_of_growth_cycle in lean/Cycle.lean: if the run reaches some C(65 + 2x) and every
C(65 + 2x) reaches a later one in at least one step, then the run from blank tape is at such a configuration at
later and later steps, so it is still running at every step: the machine never halts.
Why only the parity of r matters
The claim behind the symbolic period can be watched on the real machine for small r: start from C(r) for two odd
values of r and compare the two runs event by event. Up to the last block the two tapes are the same, and the last
blocks keep their difference. Start one of them from an even r and the tapes part at once; C(r) with r even halts,

sections.heading: Apply the growth cycle yourself
sections.html: Once the left part of the tape has reached its recurring state, the run is one rule repeated: the last block gains 321,042,928 words and everything left of it comes back exactly. Press the button to follow the orbit on the number r alone.

sections.heading: It never halts
html: Started on a blank tape, 1RB0RC_0RC1RC_0LD0RA_1LE0LF_0LA1LC_---1LA runs for ever. From step
1,818,198,163,340,705 on its run is the growth cycle: C(r) comes back as C(r + 321,042,928) after 116,320,154
arrivals of state E at the left end, and so on without end.
The Lean theorem is nonhalt : ¬ HaltsFromBlank in lean/Replay.lean, ledger level
native_decide. What it rests on, exactly:
• The Lean kernel checks the definitions of the machine, the soundness of the symbolic executor
lean/Exec.lean), the 31 shift rules (lean/ExecData.lean, each by rfl) and the
• Fourteen evaluations by native_decide, which trust Lean's compiler as well as its kernel:
the twelve cycle rules (rule0_ok … rule11_ok, from 422 to 201,007 executor moves
each), the arrival from blank tape (arrive_run, 5,037,044 moves) and the period
Quot.sound and these fourteen evaluations; there is no sorry.
• Not used: any simulator outside Lean. The executor's strategy (which rule, how many times, how to
re-bracket the tape) is not trusted; only its soundness is, and that is proved.
• Not stated in Lean: the numbers of steps and events, such as the step 1,818,198,163,340,705 at which
C(16,797,709) is first reached; Lean says only "reaches, in at least one step". Those counts come from
The short cycle rules can be checked by the kernel alone (decide +kernel was tried on rule 4, 422
moves, and rule 11, 3,255 moves); the drain rule and the two long runs have not been, so there is no kernel-only
proof of nonhalt yet. A second proof of the same statement, in Coq on top of busycoq
(coq/H65826.v, nonhalt : ~ halts tm c0), evaluates all its runs inside Coq's kernel with
vm_compute and reports no axioms; the ledger lists it as kernel level.
